listings.name: CopyFlow

tools.name: copyflow_record
tools.description: Author a routine from a 2-step demo: step 1 fetches JSON from a URL, step 2 appends a row of values to a target. CopyFlow saves the recording trace, generalizes it into a parameterized routine with the user's Claude, and shows it on the Review view for the user to confirm. Returns the compiled routine JSON (NOT yet confirmed — confirming is the user's standing grant).

inputSchema.fetchUrl: string — the URL step 1 fetches JSON from. Required.
inputSchema.appendTarget: string — where step 2 appends the row (a sheet id / connector target). Required.
inputSchema.appendValues: string — the new row's values, comma-separated or a JSON array. Optional.
inputSchema.title: string — a name for the routine. Optional.
inputSchema.fetchIntent: string — plain-language description of step 1. Optional.
inputSchema.appendIntent: string — plain-language description of step 2. Optional.

listings.author: third-party · Hacker News (public Algolia API)

tools.name: search_news
tools.description: Find trending or recent stories on Hacker News by topic — the front-page pulse for tech and AI news. Great for 'what's trending in AI', 'latest on <topic>', 'top HN stories'. Returns titles, points, comments and links.

inputSchema.query: string — the topic to search, e.g. AI (optional; omit for the front page)

inside: Trending & recent Hacker News stories by topic
Titles, points, comments, links
Great for 'find me trending AI news'
No account, no key — the public Hacker News API

listings.name: Web Search
listings.tagline: Search the open web — titles, sources, snippets. No key, runs on your machine.
listings.author: third-party · Wikipedia + DuckDuckGo (public APIs)

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the open web for a topic and get titles, sources, and snippets — the public web's answers, no key. Great for 'what is <x>', 'latest on <topic>', 'find <thing>', 'search the web for …'. Merges Wikipedia + DuckDuckGo instant answers. Returns ranked results with links.

inputSchema.query: string — what to search for, e.g. apple vision pro

inside: Live web results by topic — titles, sources, snippets
Wikipedia + DuckDuckGo instant answers, merged
Great for 'search the web for …' and 'what is …'
No account, no key — public web APIs, runs locally
